tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Check connection
tools.description: Reports which CloseSEO account and mode the client is connected as, plus the token scopes and the credit balance (the balance is null on a self-hosted server). Free: no DataForSEO call is made. Use it to confirm the connection works.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: Show projects
tools.description: Returns every project as {id, name, domain, locationCode, languageCode}. Free, no DataForSEO call. Run it first whenever another tool needs a `projectId`, and pass the `id` of the project you want. The location and language are the project's default market, used by tools when a call leaves them out. Each project also carries a link to its page in the app.

tools.name: create_project
tools.title: Add project
tools.description: Creates a project and returns {id, name, domain, locationCode, languageCode, url}; pass the new `id` as `projectId` to other tools. Free, no DataForSEO call. Only a name is required; add a domain and a default market if known (a languageCode needs a locationCode). Run list_projects first so you do not create a duplicate.

domain.description: Optional website of the project as a bare host such as "example.com" (no scheme, no path). It becomes the default target for domain, backlink and rank-tracking tools.

locationCode.description: Optional DataForSEO location code for the default market, for example 2840 for the United States or 2504 for Morocco. Defaults to the United States when left out.

languageCode.description: Optional language code such as "en" or "fr". Needs a locationCode; when omitted it is taken from the location.

organizationId.description: Not supported by CloseSEO, which has a single owner and no organizations. Leave it out; sending it is rejected.

tools.name: get_project_context
tools.title: Read project memory
tools.description: Returns what CloseSEO remembers about the project: the business overview, goal, positioning and writing style, any custom sections, the competitor and key-page lists and the latest research-log entries. Free. Load it before SEO work so you start from what the user has already said, and scan the research log so you do not pay twice for the same question. A section reported as missing is a prompt to ask the user and store the answer with update_project_context.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

tools.name: update_project_context
tools.title: Edit project memory
tools.description: Edits the project's shared memory, which the app, the built-in assistant and other agents all read. Free. Send a list of patch operations: write or clear a section, add or remove a custom section, competitors, key pages or research-log entries. Sections hold prose (about 4,000 characters at most); competitors and key pages are short curated lists (100 each); appendResearchLog notes research that has already been paid for. Look at the current context first to find what to remove, and confirm facts with the user before saving them.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

customSection.description: Lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, for instance 'launch-plan'; no underscores or spaces. The same slug identifies the section when you edit or delete it.

deleteCustomSection.description: Lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, for instance 'launch-plan'; no underscores or spaces. The same slug identifies the section when you edit or delete it.

updates.description: A list of edits applied one after another. To empty a built-in section send {section: "current_goal", content: ""}. {deleteCustomSection: "slug"} drops a custom one. removeCompetitors expects domains, removeKeyPages expects URLs, removeResearchLog expects entry IDs (all visible in the project context). A competitor or page whose domain or URL is already listed is overwritten, and research-log entries get today's date from the server.

tools.name: list_saved_keywords
tools.title: Browse saved keywords
tools.description: Returns the project's saved keywords with the metrics stored with them (volume, difficulty, CPC) and their tags. Free: it reads CloseSEO's own database, not DataForSEO. Every row carries the ID that remove_saved_keywords needs. To fetch one segment, filter by tag; several tags match a keyword that has any of them.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

search.description: Only return keywords containing this text.

tags.description: Only return keywords carrying at least one of these tag names.

limit.description: How many rows to return at most. Default 100.

tools.name: remove_saved_keywords
tools.title: Delete saved keywords
tools.description: Deletes keywords from the project's saved list by row ID, permanently. Free. IDs that do not exist, belong to another project or repeat are skipped, and deletedCount says how many rows were really removed. The rank-tracking keyword list is separate and untouched; use remove_rank_tracking_keywords for that.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

savedKeywordIds.description: Row IDs of the saved keywords to delete, taken from the `id` field of list_saved_keywords.

tools.name: research_keywords
tools.title: Keyword research for several seeds
tools.description: Researches 1 to 5 seed keywords in one call and returns, for each seed, related keywords with search volume, difficulty, CPC and intent. Paid per seed: the price rises with resultLimit, a thin seed triggers an extra fallback lookup, and countries served only from Google Ads data cost a flat amount and come without difficulty or intent. A failing seed is reported on its own and does not fail the others.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

locationName.description: Optionally narrow to a city, county or region of the seed's country to get local volumes. First run search_serp_locations and pass the locationName exactly as returned. Volume, CPC and competition then describe that area, while ideas, difficulty and intent stay national. Adds a charge per seed.

seeds.description: One to five seeds. Each is researched on its own and returns related keywords with volume, difficulty and CPC. Prefer one call with several seeds over several single-seed calls.

resultLimit.description: Most keywords to return for each seed; default 150. The default mode blends two data sources and lists a keyword found in both only once.

includeClickstreamData.description: Sharpen volumes with clickstream data, which splits the groups of close variants (plurals, misspellings) that Google Ads reports together. Doubles the price of each seed. Default false. Has no effect where only Google Ads data is available.

groupKeywords.description: Include near-duplicate variants that share one volume, CPC and competition figure. false (default) returns only the main keyword of each group; true returns the variants too. This changes which keywords are listed, not how metrics are estimated, so never add up shared volumes. Has no effect where only Google Ads data is available.

tools.name: save_keywords
tools.title: Store keywords
tools.description: Adds keywords to the project's saved list. Free. Saving a keyword that is already saved changes nothing. Tags named in the call are created if missing and, by default, added to the existing ones; tagMode=replace first strips the keyword's current tags, which suits regrouping keywords by page or topic. Ask the user before adding or replacing tags in bulk.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

metrics.description: Optional figures to store alongside the keywords: take keyword, searchVolume, keywordDifficulty, cpc, competition and intent from rows of research_keywords or get_keyword_metrics (monthlySearches is optional). Entries are paired with keywords through the keyword field.

tags.description: Optional tags to put on every keyword being saved. Get the user's explicit approval first, particularly for large batches or tag names that do not exist yet.

tagMode.description: How the tags are applied: append (default) adds to each keyword's existing tags, replace clears them first.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_domain_overview
tools.title: Domain overview
tools.description: Summarises a domain's organic footprint: estimated organic traffic, number of ranking keywords, backlinks and referring domains. Start domain research here, then call get_domain_keyword_suggestions for the keyword list itself. Paid per call (typically a few hundred credits); results are kept for 12 hours per domain.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

domain.description: Domain or URL to analyse, for example 'example.com'.

scope.description: Which part of the site to analyse: 'domain' (the host alone), 'subdomains' (the host and every subdomain), 'subfolder' (a path and everything below it) or 'exact_url' (a single page). A bare domain defaults to 'subdomains'; an input with a path defaults to 'subfolder'. The overview figures always cover the host plus subdomains and are labelled when a narrower scope was asked for; use get_ranked_keywords with a scope for keyword data limited to that scope.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_domain_keyword_suggestions
tools.title: Domain keyword list
tools.description: Lists the organic keywords a domain ranks for, with positions and the metrics available. Use it after get_domain_overview to see the detailed keyword list of a competitor or reference site. Paid per call (typically a few hundred credits); results are kept for 12 hours.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

domain.description: Competitor or reference domain or URL whose keywords you want.

scope.description: Which part of the site to use: 'domain' (the host alone), 'subdomains' (the host and every subdomain), 'subfolder' (a path and everything below it) or 'exact_url' (a single page). A bare domain defaults to 'subdomains'; an input with a path defaults to 'subfolder'.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_backlinks_overview
tools.title: Backlink summary
tools.description: Summarises a backlink profile: total backlinks, referring domains and the top referring domains. Paid per call (a page costs less than a domain). A bare domain defaults to scope 'subdomains'; pass 'domain' to leave subdomains out of the totals. A target with a path defaults to 'subfolder', whose counts are derived from filtered backlink totals and therefore carry no rank, trend or referring-domain breakdown. Trend history always includes subdomains, a limit of the data provider. The DataForSEO account must have the Backlinks API enabled.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

target.description: Domain or URL to analyse, such as 'example.com' or 'https://example.com/blog'.

scope.description: Which part of the site to analyse: 'domain' (the host alone), 'subdomains' (the host and every subdomain), 'subfolder' (a path and everything below it) or 'exact_url' (a single page). A bare domain defaults to 'subdomains'; an input with a path defaults to 'subfolder'. 'page' is an old alias for 'exact_url'. Subfolder counts come from filtered totals, so rank, trends and the referring-domain breakdown are not available for them.

hideSpam.description: Leave out referring domains that look like spam. Default true.

tools.name: get_backlinks_profile
tools.title: Backlink rows
tools.description: Returns one page of individual backlinks for a domain or page: the linking URL, the page it points to, anchor text, dofollow or nofollow, authority and spam signals, and whether the link is lost or broken. Supports filters, sorting, a one-link-per-domain mode and paging. Paid per page of results. The DataForSEO account must have the Backlinks API enabled.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

target.description: Domain or URL to analyse, such as 'example.com' or 'https://example.com/blog'.

scope.description: Which part of the site to analyse: 'domain' (the host alone), 'subdomains' (the host and every subdomain), 'subfolder' (a path and everything below it) or 'exact_url' (a single page). A bare domain defaults to 'subdomains'; an input with a path defaults to 'subfolder'. 'page' is an old alias for 'exact_url'. Subfolder counts come from filtered totals, so rank, trends and the referring-domain breakdown are not available for them.

sortField.description: Field to sort the backlink rows by.

filters.description: Narrow the backlink rows: terms the source URL must or must not contain, authority and spam ranges, dofollow or nofollow, whether lost or broken links are shown, or one exact referring domain (domainFrom).

mode.description: How links are grouped: one_per_domain keeps only the strongest link of each referring domain, as_is returns every backlink row.

hideSpam.description: Hide links whose spam score is 40 or more (default true). Links with an unknown score stay visible. The score is a rough signal, not a verdict on a link; set false to see every matching link. The provider caps filter conditions: with this on you may use six (two for subfolders), with it off eight (four for subfolders), and every include or exclude term and every numeric bound counts as one.

tools.name: get_serp_results
tools.title: Live Google results
tools.description: Fetches live Google organic results for 1 to 10 keywords, so you can see who ranks for a query, check competitors, compare result pages or collect source URLs before planning content. Returns the first `depth` rows for each keyword (default 20). Paid per keyword, and the price grows with depth. Nothing is stored in CloseSEO. A keyword that fails is reported separately and the rest still return.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

keyword.description: The search query to fetch results for.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

locationName.description: Optional city, county or region within the query's country, to get a local result page. Run search_serp_locations first and pass its locationName unchanged. Costs the same as a national query.

queries.description: One to ten queries. Prefer one call with several queries over many single-query calls.

depth.description: Number of result rows to read for each keyword: 10, 20, ... up to 100, default 20. Google offers no offset, so reading deeper also re-reads the top rows and each extra 10 adds to the price. Increase it only if you need positions past the 20th.

tools.name: search_serp_locations
tools.title: Find SERP locations
tools.description: Finds the exact DataForSEO name for a city, county or region (up to 50 results). Send the chosen `locationName` untouched to create_rank_tracker for tracking in that place, or to research_keywords for local volumes. Free.

query.description: Place name, for example "Catonsville" or "Portland OR".

countryCode.description: Two-letter ISO country code, for example "us".

tools.name: create_rank_tracker
tools.title: Set up rank tracker
tools.description: Sets up a rank tracker for a project. A tracker with no keywords costs nothing and checks nothing, but once keywords are added a daily, weekly or monthly one spends credits on each run. Defaults: the project's domain and market, mobile devices, depth 40, manual schedule. Price it with estimate_rank_tracker_cost before adding keywords to a scheduled tracker or launching a live run, and look at get_rank_tracker first to avoid a duplicate. For tracking at city level, run search_serp_locations and send its locationName unchanged.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

domain.description: The domain to track, by default the project's own. A hostname or URL is accepted; only the plain hostname is stored.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

locationName.description: Exact DataForSEO location name for city-level tracking, such as "Catonsville,Maryland,United States". It must come from search_serp_locations; free-form text like "Catonsville, MD" is rejected.

devices.description: Which devices to check. Default mobile.

serpDepth.description: How many Google results to look through. Default 40.

scheduleInterval.description: How often to check. Default manual, so creating a tracker can never cause later spending; scheduled checks do use credits.

scheduleTime.description: When scheduled checks run. Send the user's timeZone with it and the local time is converted for you; the result is fixed in UTC and moves by an hour when clocks change. Leave it out unless the user wants a particular time, because the default spreads checks over quiet hours. Daily checks run at this time every day, weekly checks on the chosen weekday, monthly checks on the last day of the month. A check begins shortly after the chosen time. Not allowed with a manual schedule.

weekday.description: Day of the week, 0 for Sunday. Needed for weekly schedules and ignored otherwise.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone that the weekday, hour and minute refer to, such as "America/New_York". Default UTC.

tools.name: get_rank_tracker
tools.title: View rank trackers
tools.description: Read-only view of rank trackers. Given a `trackerId` it returns the tracker's settings and the newest result for every keyword, including the `trackingKeywordId` needed to remove one; without it, it lists the project's trackers. Free. If none exists, create one with create_rank_tracker, then manage it with add_rank_tracking_keywords, remove_rank_tracking_keywords, estimate_rank_tracker_cost and run_rank_tracker. `lastCheckedAt` tells you how fresh the positions are.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

trackerId.description: ID of one rank tracker. Leave it out to list all trackers of the project.

tools.name: add_rank_tracking_keywords
tools.title: Add keywords to rank tracker
tools.description: Adds keywords to an existing tracker. The edit is free and neither checks positions nor fetches metrics, but on a scheduled tracker every later recurring check spends credits. For a scheduled tracker, first call estimate_rank_tracker_cost with additionalKeywords, tell the user the recurring cost and the live-fallback caveat, and send the figure they approved as maxEstimatedScheduledCheckCredits. That figure records approval only and is not a spending limit: queued tasks that are rejected, fail or time out can fall back to separately billed live checks. Keywords that are already tracked, or repeated in the request, are skipped; `added` counts what was inserted.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

trackerId.description: ID of the tracker, from get_rank_tracker.

keywords.description: Keywords to start tracking. Ones already tracked, or repeated, are skipped.

matchCase.description: Keep each keyword exactly as typed instead of lowercasing it (default false). Useful for brand names whose results change with capitalisation; a cased keyword is tracked, and charged, separately from its lowercase form.

maxEstimatedScheduledCheckCredits.description: Credits per scheduled check, as estimated by estimate_rank_tracker_cost with additionalKeywords, that the user has approved. Required for scheduled trackers. It records approval only and is not a cap: a live fallback can add separately billed credits.

tools.name: remove_rank_tracking_keywords
tools.title: Drop rank tracker keywords
tools.description: Stops tracking the given keywords by trackingKeywordId. Free; past results are kept. IDs that are unknown, outdated, belong to another tracker or repeat are skipped, and `removed` counts the keywords really deleted from this tracker.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

trackerId.description: ID of the tracker, from get_rank_tracker.

keywordIds.description: IDs of the tracked keywords to remove: the `trackingKeywordId` values from get_rank_tracker.

tools.name: estimate_rank_tracker_cost
tools.title: Price a rank tracker
tools.description: Prices a rank tracker without spending anything or starting a check. The live figure is the cost of one run_rank_tracker check. For a scheduled tracker the answer also gives the queued cost of one check and a rough monthly total. Pass additionalKeywords to see the cost after adding them. Scheduled figures are estimates, not limits: queued tasks that are rejected, fail or time out may fall back to separately billed live checks.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

trackerId.description: ID of the tracker, from get_rank_tracker.

additionalKeywordCount.description: How many keywords you intend to add, priced as ordinary keywords. Use additionalKeywords instead when you know the keywords.

additionalKeywords.description: Keywords you plan to add. Provide them before adding to a scheduled tracker to see its price per check and per month; a keyword with a search operator such as site: is charged five times. Takes priority over additionalKeywordCount.

tools.name: run_rank_tracker
tools.title: Check rankings now
tools.description: Starts a live position check of every keyword on every configured device. It spends credits, so call estimate_rank_tracker_cost first, show the user the figure and pass what they approved as maxCostCredits; a fresh estimate above it is refused. If a check is already running, its run ID is returned and nothing new is started or billed. The schedule is not changed.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

trackerId.description: ID of the tracker, from get_rank_tracker.

maxCostCredits.description: Highest credit amount the user accepted after seeing estimate_rank_tracker_cost. If a new estimate comes out higher, the run is refused.

tools.name: get_ranked_keywords
tools.title: Keywords a site ranks for
tools.description: Lists the keywords a domain or page ranks for in one market, with URL, position, search volume, CPC, intent and traffic estimate. Takes country-level DataForSEO Labs location and language codes. Use it as evidence for strategy; use get_domain_overview for the overall footprint. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

target.description: Domain (no protocol or www) or full page URL whose ranked keywords you want.

scope.description: Which part of the site to use: 'domain' (the host alone), 'subdomains' (the host and every subdomain), 'subfolder' (a path and everything below it) or 'exact_url' (a single page). A bare domain defaults to 'subdomains'; an input with a path defaults to 'subfolder'.

market.description: Old selector limited to the US. Prefer locationCode and languageCode for any Labs market. A given locationCode wins; with neither, the project's market is used.

country.description: Country choice. Only the United States can be named here.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO Labs location code at country level. Defaults to the project's market and takes priority over the old market object.

languageCode.description: Language to use with locationCode. When locationCode differs from the project's market it defaults to that location's main language.

resultTypes.description: Which SERP result types to include. Default: organic and paid.

minSearchVolume.description: Only keep keywords with at least this monthly search volume.

maxRank.description: Only keep keywords ranking at this position or higher (a smaller number is better).

excludeBrandTerms.description: Drop keywords that contain any of these brand terms.

sortBy.description: How to order the rows. Default search_volume.

limit.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 100. Default 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip, for paging.

tools.name: find_serp_competitors
tools.title: Find competing domains
tools.description: Compares the domains that compete for a set of keywords in Google results, in a country-level DataForSEO Labs market. Takes location and language codes; it is not a radius-based local SEO tool. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

keywords.description: Keywords whose result pages are compared, 1 to 100.

market.description: Old selector limited to the US. Prefer locationCode and languageCode for any Labs market. A given locationCode wins; with neither, the project's market is used.

country.description: Country choice. Only the United States can be named here.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO Labs location code at country level. Defaults to the project's market and takes priority over the old market object.

languageCode.description: Language to use with locationCode. When locationCode differs from the project's market it defaults to that location's main language.

resultTypes.description: Which SERP result types to include. Default: organic and local_pack.

excludeDomains.description: Domains to leave out, for example the user's own site.

includeSubdomains.description: Treat subdomains as part of the same competitor domain.

sortBy.description: How to order the competitors. Default visibility.

limit.description: Most competitors to return, 1 to 100. Default 50.

offset.description: How many rows to skip, for paging.

tools.name: search_local_businesses
tools.title: Find local businesses
tools.description: Finds local business listings around a coordinate, optionally filtered by rating, number of reviews and whether the listing is claimed. Use it to discover local competitors, candidates or unclaimed listings. It does not check Maps rankings or fetch Q&A. Each row is brief (identity, contact, rating, claim status); get_business_profile gives one business in full. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

query.description: Business name, or part of it, to match.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point to search around.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius in whole kilometres; fractions are rounded.

near.description: The point and radius to search around.

categories.description: Business categories to filter by, for example 'pizza_restaurant'.

minRating.description: Only return businesses rated at least this, 1 to 5.

minReviews.description: Minimum number of Google reviews a business must have.

isClaimed.description: Filter on whether the owner has claimed the listing. false shows unclaimed listings, which make outreach prospects.

sortBy.description: How to order the rows. Default relevance.

limit.description: Most businesses to return, 1 to 50. Default 20.

offset.description: How many rows to skip, for paging.

tools.name: get_local_serp_results
tools.title: Maps and Local Finder results
tools.description: Fetches a single Google Maps or Local Finder result page as seen from a coordinate. Returns slimmed provider rows (identity, rank, rating, categories, hours) with the rank fields untouched, so the caller decides how to recognise a target business. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

keyword.description: The query to run in Google Maps or Local Finder.

latitude.description: Latitude the result page is fetched from.

longitude.description: Longitude the result page is fetched from.

zoom.description: Map zoom from 4 to 18; a higher zoom covers a smaller area.

near.description: The coordinate, with an optional map zoom, the result page is fetched from.

searchType.description: Which local result page to fetch. Default maps.

device.description: Device the page is rendered for. Default mobile, the same as get_local_rank_grid.

depth.description: How many results to fetch, 1 to 100. Default 20.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_google_business_questions
tools.title: Google business Q&A
tools.description: Fetches the questions and answers on one business's Google profile, found by businessName, cid or placeId and a coordinate. Call it only when you actually need Q&A evidence. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

businessName.description: The business name as Google shows it. Give exactly one of businessName, cid or placeId.

cid.description: Google's business CID, as found in get_local_serp_results rows. The most precise identifier.

placeId.description: Google Maps place_id, as found in get_local_serp_results rows.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point to search around.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius in whole kilometres; fractions are rounded.

near.description: The point and radius to search around.

depth.description: Most Q&A rows to fetch, 1 to 100. Default 20.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_business_profile
tools.title: Google business profile
tools.description: Reads a single Google Business Profile: primary and extra categories, star rating with the review count and star breakdown, address, phone number, website, whether the owner has claimed it, opening hours and number of photos. Good for auditing your own listing or sizing up a competitor. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

businessName.description: The business name as Google shows it. Give exactly one of businessName, cid or placeId.

cid.description: Google's business CID, as found in get_local_serp_results rows. The most precise identifier.

placeId.description: Google Maps place_id, as found in get_local_serp_results rows.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point to search around.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the point in kilometres, 0.2 to 199. Default 10.

near.description: A point to start from. Use it if the business name is ambiguous; otherwise locationCode is sufficient.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Ignored when `near` is given; otherwise the project's market is used.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_business_reviews
tools.title: Google business reviews
tools.description: Gathers a business's Google reviews with rating, reviewer, text and whether the owner replied, for comparing review counts with competitors and finding unanswered reviews. Most calls finish immediately. When the queued job is still running the answer is status 'processing' with a taskId; call again with that taskId after 30 to 60 seconds to get the reviews without paying again. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

businessName.description: The business name as Google shows it. Give exactly one of businessName, cid or placeId.

cid.description: Google's business CID, as found in get_local_serp_results rows. The most precise identifier.

placeId.description: Google Maps place_id, as found in get_local_serp_results rows.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point to search around.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the point in kilometres, 0.2 to 199. Default 10.

near.description: A point to start from. Use it if the business name is ambiguous; otherwise locationCode is sufficient.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Ignored when `near` is given; otherwise the project's market is used.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

depth.description: How many reviews to collect, 10 to 200. Default 20. Billed in blocks of 10 reviews (blocks of 20 when includeOtherSources is true).

sortBy.description: How to order the reviews. Default newest. Ignored when includeOtherSources is true, because that mode cannot be sorted.

includeOtherSources.description: Also gather the reviews that Google lists from other websites (Yelp, Tripadvisor, Trustpilot). Default false. Each review costs more and the results cannot be sorted.

taskId.description: Picks up an earlier call that answered "processing". Send back the taskId unchanged (it looks like "google:<id>" or "extended:<id>" and already says which kind of collection it is). Collecting costs nothing extra.

tools.name: get_business_updates
tools.title: Google business posts
tools.description: Gathers the posts (updates, offers, events) a Google Business Profile has published, to judge how active and current a profile is, whether yours or a competitor's. It normally completes within the call; if it answers 'processing' it includes a taskId, and calling again with it after 30 to 60 seconds fetches the outcome free of charge. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

businessName.description: The business name as Google shows it. Give exactly one of businessName, cid or placeId.

cid.description: Google's business CID, as found in get_local_serp_results rows. The most precise identifier.

placeId.description: Google Maps place_id, as found in get_local_serp_results rows.

latitude.description: Latitude of the point to search around.

longitude.description: Longitude of the point to search around.

radiusKm.description: Search radius around the point in kilometres, 0.2 to 199. Default 10.

near.description: A point to start from. Use it if the business name is ambiguous; otherwise locationCode is sufficient.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Ignored when `near` is given; otherwise the project's market is used.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

depth.description: How many posts to collect, 10 to 100. Default 10.

taskId.description: Picks up an earlier call that answered "processing". Send back the taskId unchanged. Collecting costs nothing extra.

tools.name: list_business_categories
tools.title: Business category list
tools.description: Lists the Google Business categories DataForSEO knows, most used first. Use it to find valid category names for search_local_businesses, such as 'pizza_restaurant'. Free; the full list is kept for 7 days.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

query.description: Text to look for inside category names, ignoring case, for example 'plumb'.

limit.description: Most categories to return, 1 to 200. Default 50.

tools.name: get_local_rank_grid
tools.title: Local rank grid
tools.description: Runs one Google Maps search for each point of a square grid centred on a coordinate and shows the target business's position at every point, together with how many results the point returned and who came first. This shows how far the business's Maps visibility extends. The cost is one search per point (gridSize squared: 9 for the default 3x3, 25 for 5x5). Paid per grid point.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

keyword.description: The query to run on Google Maps at each grid point.

cid.description: Matches a result whose cid equals this value. The most dependable option.

placeId.description: Matches a result whose place_id equals this value.

name.description: Matches a result whose title contains this text, ignoring case. Only used when cid and placeId find nothing.

target.description: The business to find in every result set. Give at least one of cid, placeId or name.

center.description: The coordinate the grid is centred on, usually the shop or office.

gridSize.description: Number of points along one side: 3 (9 searches) or 5 (25 searches). Default 3.

spacingKm.description: Distance between neighbouring points in km. Default 2.

device.description: Device the pages are rendered for. Default mobile.

zoom.description: Map zoom used at every point. By default it is worked out from spacingKm and the latitude so that each point's view covers the spacing between points; set it only when you need a particular view.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

tools.name: get_keyword_metrics
tools.title: Keyword metrics lookup
tools.description: Looks up search volume, keyword difficulty (KD), intent, CPC, competition and monthly trend for up to 700 keywords you already have, in one call. Use it to rank candidate keywords, including Search Console queries that are close to page one, by real demand and difficulty. In countries served only from Google Ads data (such as Iceland) KD and intent come back null. Paid per call.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

locationCode.description: DataForSEO location code. Defaults to the project's market (see list_projects). Some countries, such as Iceland (2352), are served from Google Ads data only: volume, CPC and trends work, but difficulty, intent and domain analytics are not available there.

languageCode.description: Language code such as 'en', 'es' or 'vi'. Defaults to the language of the project's market.

includeMonthlyTrends.description: Include the monthly search-volume rows. Default true.

includeClickstreamData.description: Sharpen volumes with clickstream data, which splits the groups of close variants (plurals, misspellings) that Google Ads reports together. Doubles the price of the call. Default false. Has no effect where only Google Ads data is available.

sortBy.description: How to order the rows. Default search_volume.

tools.name: get_search_console_performance
tools.title: Search Console performance
tools.description: Queries Search Analytics for the project's connected Search Console property and returns clicks, impressions, CTR and average position grouped by query, page, country, device or date. As first-party data it shows what already ranks, queries that nearly rank and pages with genuine demand. Google orders by clicks and cannot filter by position, so minPosition, maxPosition and minImpressions are applied on our side to the top 1000 rows of the period; use them instead of pulling everything. ctr runs from 0 to 1; position is a 1-based average that is missing for 'discover' and 'googleNews' because Google does not report it (not an error); dates follow Pacific Time and the last ~3 days may be incomplete. Only the property already linked to the project is read, with the Google account stored in that link. Read-only and free.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

dimensions.description: Dimensions that define each row; default ['query']. Choose ['page'] for top pages, ['query','page'] to pair queries with pages and detect cannibalisation, or ['date'] for a time series.

dateRange.description: Shortcut for the period (default last_28_days). It ends about 3 days ago because Search Console data lags, and it is ignored when startDate and endDate are both given. Data goes back at most 16 months.

startDate.description: First day of the period as YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific Time. Use together with endDate.

endDate.description: Last day of the period as YYYY-MM-DD in Pacific Time. Use together with startDate.

filters.description: Conditions that must all be true. To get one page's queries, use dimensions ['query'] with [{dimension:'page',operator:'equals',expression:'https://example.com/post'}].

rowLimit.description: Rows per call, default 250, at most 1000. Rows come sorted by clicks, highest first; when hasMore is true, fetch the next block with startRow.

startRow.description: Row offset to start from, for paging.

minPosition.description: Keep rows whose average position is this number or larger. For queries near page one try minPosition 5, maxPosition 20 and minImpressions 50.

maxPosition.description: Keep only rows whose average position is at most this number.

minImpressions.description: Keep only rows with at least this many impressions.

type.description: Kind of search to report on. Default web.

dataState.description: 'all' (default) also counts the newest data, which may still be incomplete.

tools.name: inspect_urls
tools.title: Search Console URL inspection
tools.description: Reports what Search Console already knows about as many as 10 URLs in the connected property: index and coverage state, last crawl time, Google's chosen canonical versus the declared one, and mobile and rich-result verdicts. Use it to answer 'is this page indexed, and if not, why?'. Google accepts only URLs inside that property, and no live crawl happens. A failing URL is reported in place without affecting the others. Only the property already linked to the project is read, with the Google account stored in that link. Read-only and free.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

urls.description: Between one and ten absolute URLs to inspect, each inside the connected property.

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language for the inspection text, for example 'en-US'.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_organic_landing_pages
tools.title: Analytics: organic landing pages
tools.description: Reads, from the project's connected GA4 property, how organic-search landing pages perform: sessions, engagement, key events, transactions and revenue. The default period is the last 28 complete days of the property. Only the GA4 property already connected to a CloseSEO project is read, using the Google account saved with that connection. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_page_performance
tools.title: Analytics: page performance
tools.description: Reads page views, users, engagement time and key events for the pages of the connected GA4 property. By default only Organic Search traffic counts; set channel to all for every channel.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_key_events
tools.title: Analytics: key events
tools.description: Reads the active GA4 key events with their counts and users, broken down by event or by organic landing page; the event breakdown can be compared with the previous period. Only the GA4 property already connected to a CloseSEO project is read, using the Google account saved with that connection. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: get_search_opportunities
tools.title: Search opportunities
tools.description: Joins Search Console pages that rank between positions 4 and 20 with how those pages perform as GA4 organic landing pages, then ranks each match by demand, business value and how reachable the gain is. Pages without a match are still listed, unscored. Both the Search Console and GA4 properties must already be linked to the project, and the Google accounts stored in those links are used. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_organic_overview
tools.title: Analytics: organic overview
tools.description: Answers whether organic traffic is getting better: headline sessions, users, engagement, key events, transactions and revenue, compared with an equally long previous period, plus a daily or weekly trend. Only the GA4 property already connected to a CloseSEO project is read, using the Google account saved with that connection. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.description: Compares how sessions arrive, by channel group, source/medium or campaign, with sessions, users, engagement, key events, transactions and revenue. The previous-period comparison exists for channel groups; source/medium also reports diagnostics on how well traffic is attributed. Only the GA4 property already connected to a CloseSEO project is read, using the Google account saved with that connection. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_measurement_health
tools.title: Analytics: measurement health
tools.description: Reviews how the connected property is configured for measurement: its data streams and web measurement IDs, enhanced-measurement options, key events and custom definitions.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

tools.name: get_google_analytics_ecommerce_performance
tools.title: Analytics: ecommerce performance
tools.description: Reads views, add-to-cart units, purchases and revenue per product, or transactions and purchase revenue per landing page. The result also states whether ecommerce activity was detected, absent or unknown, and landing pages can be restricted to those with transactions. Organic Search is the default channel.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.title: Analytics: site search
tools.description: Reads the on-site search terms visitors typed, with the number of search events, users, sessions and engaged sessions and the engagement rate. GA4 site-search measurement must be enabled.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.title: Analytics: audience breakdown
tools.description: Reads users, sessions, engagement and key events by device, by country or by new versus returning visitors; device and new-versus-returning can be compared with the previous period. There are no demographic or user-level dimensions. Only the GA4 property already connected to a CloseSEO project is read, using the Google account saved with that connection. Read-only and free of CloseSEO credits.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

startDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

endDate.description: First day (inclusive) as YYYY-MM-DD. Send startDate and endDate together.

tools.name: run_site_audit
tools.title: Start site audit
tools.description: Launches an audit in the background. The crawler stays on the starting origin, honours robots.txt and checks every page for SEO faults: broken links, missing or repeated titles and meta descriptions, redirect chains, canonical errors, orphan pages, thin text and others. Lighthouse can optionally be run on some pages. Check progress with get_audit_status and read findings with get_audit_issues. When the site throttles the crawler it backs off and retries, and pages it never manages to read are labelled blocked or rate-limited rather than guessed at.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

maxPages.description: How many pages the crawl may visit at most. Default 50.

renderJavaScript.description: Not supported by CloseSEO: audits fetch pages without running JavaScript, and a request with this set to true is rejected. Leave it false (the default).

runLighthouse.description: Run Lighthouse on up to 10 representative pages. Default false, because it adds several minutes. Turn it on only when the user wants performance or Core Web Vitals detail.

tools.name: list_site_audits
tools.title: Browse site audits
tools.description: Returns the project's audits newest first, with ID, URL, status, page counts and dates. Free. Use it to locate an earlier audit you want to read or delete; when no ID is given, get_audit_status only looks at the newest one.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

tools.name: delete_site_audit
tools.title: Remove site audit
tools.description: Permanently deletes one audit together with its crawled pages, issues and Lighthouse results. Free. A running audit is stopped first. Saved reports and the project's context are not affected.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

auditId.description: ID of the audit to delete, from list_site_audits or run_site_audit. Required; it never falls back to the newest audit.

tools.name: get_audit_status
tools.title: Site audit progress
tools.description: Shows how far an audit has got (phase, pages crawled, Lighthouse progress). Free: it reads CloseSEO's own records, and an audit whose crawl died is marked failed. Without an auditId the newest audit is used.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

auditId.description: ID of the audit. Defaults to the project's newest audit.

tools.name: get_audit_issues
tools.title: Site audit issue report
tools.description: Returns the issue report of a finished audit, most important first. Each issue comes with a how_to_fix describing concrete steps. Free: it reads CloseSEO's own records. Without an auditId the newest audit is used.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

auditId.description: ID of the audit. Defaults to the project's newest audit.

severity.description: Restrict the result to one severity level.

issueType.description: Only return issues of this type. Types: page_server_error, page_not_found, redirect_loop, redirect_chain, title_missing, title_too_long, title_too_short, title_duplicate, meta_description_missing, meta_description_too_long, meta_description_duplicate, h1_missing, h1_multiple, canonical_missing, canonical_points_elsewhere, noindex, images_missing_alt, low_word_count, slow_response, missing_lang, missing_viewport, mixed_content, not_https, broken_internal_link, robots_txt_missing, sitemap_missing, blocked_by_robots.

tools.name: get_audit_pages
tools.title: Site audit page list
tools.description: Returns the pages an audit crawled with their on-page data: status, title, description, word count, whether they can be indexed, depth in the site and link counts. Free; CloseSEO's own records are read. Without an auditId the newest audit is used.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

auditId.description: ID of the audit. Defaults to the project's newest audit.

fetchClass.description: Filter by how fetching the page ended: "blocked" means bot protection on the site challenged the crawler; "rate_limited" means the site answered 429 so the page could not be read.

statusCode.description: Only pages with exactly this HTTP status code.

urlContains.description: Only pages whose URL contains this text.

tools.name: save_report
tools.title: Store report
tools.description: Stores a finished HTML report in the project; it can then be read and printed in the app. Free. Reports are private when created, and replacing one leaves its sharing choice alone while updating what any public link displays. Only if the user explicitly asked for public sharing, call set_report_sharing once the save is done. Before saving, run list_reports and pass the matching reportId when redoing a report rather than adding a near-duplicate; a title already used in the project is refused. Choose a specific title (what the report covers plus its full date), write a summary with the verdict, the main action and the headline numbers, and send the slug of the skill you are following. When done, tell the user the returned url, give a one-sentence verdict and the one action that matters most, and keep the report itself out of the chat.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

title.description: Name the kind of report or its specific subject and include the complete date, e.g. "Competitive Landscape — Sep 17, 2026". Do not mention the project's own website; add another site's bare hostname only when it is not the project's site or the project has no site. Reuse this exact title for the HTML <title> and the h1. Generic labels such as "SEO Report" are not allowed. At most 120 characters.

summary.description: Markdown below 2,500 characters holding the verdict, the one action that matters most and the headline numbers. list_reports returns it, and other agents read it in place of the HTML.

html.description: The report as a single self-contained HTML document. Put all CSS inline and request nothing from outside (no CDNs, web fonts, image URLs or fetch calls): such requests are blocked when the report is displayed, as are scripts. Do not use backticks or the characters ${ anywhere, including inside CSS strings, because some clients run this value through a JavaScript template literal and either would damage the document. Submit a complete document that ends with </html>; a partial one is refused, as no earlier version could replace it. Stay below roughly 80 KB so one call can read it back; 500,000 bytes is the absolute maximum. A simple semantic page (heading, short sections, one table) is fine.

reportId.description: Leave out to start a new report. Provide an ID from list_reports to overwrite that report; no history is kept, so the previous content disappears.

skill.description: Slug of the skill that created the report (the name in the SKILL.md you follow), for example "seo-audit". The report list groups on it; leave it out and the list shows "—".

templateId.description: ID of the template you followed (see list_report_templates or the project context). Provide it only when you really used that template; the report list and page then display it in place of the skill slug.

tools.name: list_reports
tools.title: Browse reports
tools.description: Returns the project's saved reports with the most recently changed first: ID, title, skill, author, date and the opening of the summary. Free. Run it before save_report and send the ID of the report being redone, so each job leaves a single good report behind. get_report gives the full summary; fetch the HTML only when a specific passage needs editing.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

limit.description: Reports per page, most recently updated first. Default 20, at most 50.

offset.description: How many reports to skip. Leave out for the first page.

tools.name: get_report
tools.title: Read report
tools.description: Reads one saved report: title, skill, who saved it, size, the complete summary and shareUrl (null if the report is private or this server has sharing off). Reading never publishes anything; change sharing with set_report_sharing only on the user's explicit request. Free. It is the inexpensive way to learn what a report already says before you revise it; ask for includeHtml only if you need the document itself.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

reportId.description: ID of the report, from list_reports or save_report.

includeHtml.description: Return the full HTML document as well. Skip this unless one passage needs editing: a report of 80 KB costs around 20,000 tokens and many clients cut longer content. If you do request it, compare new TextEncoder().encode(html).length with htmlBytes in the reply; if your copy is shorter, the client truncated it, so point the user to the app and do not overwrite the good report with the shortened text.

tools.name: set_report_sharing
tools.title: Change report sharing
tools.description: Switches public sharing of one saved report on or off. Free. Reports begin private, so enable sharing only on an explicit request from the user, whether in the conversation or in the skill's instructions. Whoever holds shareUrl can read the newest saved version with no account. Public sharing exists in CloseSEO only when the operator has switched it on. Sending true a second time leaves the link unchanged; false revokes it, and turning it on again produces a different link. The reply carries the app url and shareUrl (null once revoked). Use get_report to read an existing link without touching access.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

reportId.description: ID of the report, from list_reports or save_report.

public.description: Required. true creates a public link that opens without an account; false revokes the link now in place. Use true only if the user has explicitly asked for public sharing, in the conversation or in the skill's instructions. Do not infer permission from what the report contains, where its research came from, or from a plain request to save it.

tools.name: delete_report
tools.title: Remove report
tools.description: Permanently deletes one saved report and disables its shared link. Free. Use list_reports to find the exact reportId. Audits, templates and project context stay.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

reportId.description: ID of the report, from list_reports or save_report.

tools.name: list_report_templates
tools.title: Browse report templates
tools.description: Returns the report templates saved in the project. Free. A template is a reusable brief (readers, section order, tone, closing line) that stands in for a skill's usual layout. Open one only when the user mentions it by name or wants that style of report; otherwise follow the skill's own layout. To apply a template, send its id as templateId to save_report. To reuse it in a different project, list it in the source project and save it again in the target.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

tools.name: save_report_template
tools.title: Store report template
tools.description: Stores a reusable report brief in the project. Free. Create one only if the user wants a template or accepts your suggestion; a single report does not need it. Run list_report_templates first and send the existing templateId to update a template instead of duplicating it. Reusing a name that already exists in the project is refused.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

templateId.description: Leave out to make a new template. Provide an ID from list_report_templates to overwrite that template's name, description and instructions.

name.description: The name the user will use to ask for it, for example "Client-ready audit summary". Up to 80 characters.

description.description: One line saying when the template applies. Agents use it to decide, so describe the occasion rather than the format. Up to 200 characters.

instructions.description: Markdown of up to 3,000 characters covering who the report is for, the order of its sections, the tone, how it ends and, if wanted, an accent colour written "accent: #1C4ED8". These override the skill's normal sections and tone, but not the HTML restrictions for reports, which still apply.

tools.name: delete_report_template
tools.title: Remove report template
tools.description: Permanently deletes one reusable report template from the project. Free. Use list_report_templates to find its templateId. Reports already saved are kept.

projectId.description: Required. ID of the project this call applies to; get it from list_projects.

templateId.description: ID of the template, from list_report_templates.
